transcript:
Header: 2025-10-07 16:00 UTC | Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Marco Diaz (Redwood SE), Ravi Menon (Redwood Solutions); Maya Patel (Orion - Sec Arch), James O'Neill (Orion - IT Ops), Priya Reddy (Orion - Compliance), Oscar Liu (Orion - App Platform)

Auto-summary: walk-through of SSO and provisioning; client has SOC 2 in scope and regional data residency needs; primary ask is RBAC templates and proof-of-concept for SCIM provisioning.

00:00:05 Lena (Redwood AE): Hi everybody, thanks for joining. quick readout of agenda, we'll start with SAML metadata and then SCIM prototyping, move to RBAC mapping and then finish with audit logs and KMS questions.
00:00:18 Maya (Orion): Sounds good. we have about an hour; I put Priya and James on for compliance / ops questions.
00:00:26 Marco (Redwood SE): Hey all, I'm Marco, I'll run the config bits and show an example mapping. apologies in advance if my screen share is a little slow.
00:00:34 James: no worries. we really want to avoid surprises — timeline is end of Q4 for pilot.

00:02:12 Lena: Quick qual question — are you already using a single IdP across the org? SAML only or also SCIM-enabled provisioning?
00:02:26 Maya: We run Okta currently, SCIM is on for a few apps but not everything. PRetry to automate where we can.
00:02:40 Priya: from a compliance perspective, we need proof that access deprovisioning is atomic and that audit trails are immutable for at least 12 months (SOC 2 requirement).
00:03:05 Marco: Good. Redwood supports SCIM v2, we can do push provisioning and delta syncs. One note: our provisioning model maps Okta groups -> Redwood roles, and we support custom attribute mapping for things like "data_residency_role".
00:03:30 Oscar: Custom attributes, can we enforce attribute-based restrictions per tenant? e.g., force EU-only models for some business units.
00:03:44 Marco: Yes; we have routing/policy rules — you can bind a role + region policy so requests under role X are routed to EU region. there are a couple of docs I'll share.

00:05:00 James: What about SAML metadata — do you need SP-initiated, IdP-initiated? we tend to do SP for admin portals but IdP for user SSO.
00:05:15 Lena: We accept both. For onboarding it's easiest to exchange a metadata XML from Okta; I'll attach our SP metadata. also we have a short runbook for Okta-specific steps.
00:05:39 Maya: Great. can you also call out required attributes? some of our apps only pass email and name.
00:05:51 Marco: Required: 'email' and 'sub' / 'userName' for account identity. For RBAC mapping we recommend sending group membership and an attribute like 'role' or 'entitlement'. if group names differ we'll provide a mapping table.

00:07:20 Priya: On audit logs — SOC 2 asks for tamper-evidence and retention. can you export logs to our SIEM? and what's retention by default?
00:07:37 Marco: Default is 90 days in the console; longer retention is available as an add-on and we've integrated with Splunk/Datadog/S3 exports. Exports are signed and we store an append-only stream; I'll caveat that the customer must configure an external bucket for long-term retention for compliance guarantees.
00:08:05 Priya: so we should plan to push to our S3 bucket in eu-west-1. any encryption caveats?
00:08:12 Marco: We support server-side encryption and customer-managed keys (KMS). If you want keys in your account, for Private deployments we can plug into your KMS/HSM. For hosted, we spin a per-customer CMK alias; there is limited cross-account key usage unless we do private deployment.
00:08:40 Maya: So for pilot do you recommend Private or Dedicated? cost vs compliance tradeoffs.
00:08:49 Lena: For strict KMS control + VPC isolation, Private is recommended. if you're just testing SSO flows and RBAC mapping a hosted sandbox with export-to-your-S3 + CMEK can be ok.

00:10:05 Oscar: Regarding RBAC, can we implement least-privilege by default and then escalate? we want to avoid giving devs broad rights.
00:10:16 Marco: We recommend role templates: Viewer, Reader, Model-Invoker, Admin. Each template is minimal by default; you can add fine-grained permissions like 'route-to-eu' or 'create-deployments'. SCIM can provision to these roles via group-to-role mapping.
00:10:35 Maya: Do you have example RoleSpecs we can copy into our governance docs?
00:10:42 Marco: Yes, I'll attach RBAC templates. note that the RBAC enforcement lives in the control plane — we also emit audit events when role bindings change.

00:12:30 James: A bit worried about orphaned service accounts after people leave. how do you recommend handling service principals?
00:12:42 Marco: Use time-bound service tokens and rotate them. For SCIM deprovisioning we can map Okta service account lifecycle so when an account is disabled it deprovisions within the next delta sync (configurable window). We also emit a 'deprovision' audit event.

00:14:00 Priya: Can you show an example of the audit log line for a role change?
00:14:12 Marco: Sure, I'll paste a sample in chat — "timestamp, actor, target, action, previous_role, new_role, request_id". (chat link: sample-audit-line.txt)
00:15:05 Maya: thanks. can logs be forwarded in near real-time to our SIEM or is it batch?
00:15:18 Marco: We support near real-time streaming to customers' ingestion endpoints (webhooks) and S3. For compliance we prefer pushing to your S3 with an immutability policy.

00:16:30 Lena: Quick callout on naming — please avoid using person emails as role names; use canonical roles and a mapping table. helps audits.
00:16:44 Maya: noted.

00:18:00 Priya: On data residency — some lines of business can't leave EU, others ok in US. how do you partition?
00:18:15 Marco: We bind projects to regions; requests with region-restricted roles are routed to region-specific serving pools. For Private deployments, you can pin a whole control plane to a region. We'll need to map which datasets/models are restricted.
00:19:05 Oscar: Are embeddings stored long-term? Any PII concerns?
00:19:13 Marco: By default we don't retain prompts/outputs beyond retention policy; we also have an opt-out for training and long-term storage. For PII, we recommend detection at the client and token redaction pre-ingest.

00:21:00 James: KMS flow — if we bring our own key, how is the plaintext handled? who has access?
00:21:12 Marco: With customer-managed keys in Private, the actual plaintext never leaves the customer's environment; Redwood stores ciphertext and requests decryption via your KMS. For hosted CMEK we have a limited key wrapping flow — it's documented in the security whitepaper.
00:21:36 Priya: Ok please send the whitepaper and the KMS integration checklist.
00:21:42 Lena: Will do.

00:23:45 Maya: On SCIM, attribute mapping — if Okta doesn't send 'department', can we fallback to group parsing?
00:23:55 Marco: Yes, we support attribute fallbacks and group parsing heuristics — not perfect but workable. We'll share mapping examples.

00:26:10 Lena: Let's talk about SAML cert rollover — what's the process?
00:26:19 Marco: We support dual-cert signing windows; you upload new cert, we validate, then set new cert active at a scheduled cutover. We also provide metadata endpoints that clients can poll.

00:28:40 Oscar: Any rate limits that could block our automation?
00:28:48 Marco: There are admin API rate limits — we'll share the numbers. For provisioning we recommend batched SCIM delta windows instead of single-user calls in high-volume migrations.

00:31:00 Priya: For SOC 2 evidence, can Redwood provide attestations of role-change audit trails?
00:31:12 Lena: Yes, we can provide exportable audit bundles for auditor review. For deeper attestation we have SOC 2 Type II report available under NDA.
00:31:28 Priya: we'll request that under our procurement flow.

00:33:05 James: Network — for Private pilot we'll need to test connectivity to your control plane. are there IP ranges to allow?
00:33:18 Marco: Yes, we'll provide a minimal egress list and a set of TLS fingerprinting certs. For Private on-prem we can do peering or direct connect.

00:35:00 Maya: One weird thing — some of our teams use service accounts programmatically with long TTLs. how do we ensure they are audited?
00:35:12 Marco: Token audit events are emitted; we also have token binding to a service principal with rotation policies. we'll help you set the TTL policy via an org config.

00:37:40 Lena: Recap: we'll send SP metadata and SCIM templates; Marco attaches RBAC templates and sample audit lines; customer provides 10 pilot users and attribute map; schedule test week. any blockers?
00:38:00 Maya: none from us. Priya: procurement will ask for SOC 2 and data processing agreement (DPA).
00:38:10 Lena: We'll attach SOC 2 and DPA drafts.

00:40:00 James: Can we run an end-to-end SSO test during the pilot with a live model call to verify end-to-end encryption and routing?
00:40:12 Marco: Yep, we'll spin a canary model and run a test traffic pattern. we'll collect KMS logs and audit events and share results.

00:42:20 Priya: timeline confirmation — pilot start target 10/20, pilot duration 2 weeks, compliance review parallel.
00:42:32 Lena: Sounds right.

00:44:00 Maya: A tiny nit: in your docs you call it 'Redwood Private' and sometimes 'Redwood Privet' in the older PDF — watch for typos.
00:44:12 Marco: ha noted. our docs have a few legacy names; we'll standardize in the docs we send.

00:46:00 Lena: I'll follow up with an email that includes the attachments: SP metadata, RBAC templates, SCIM examples, SOC2/whitepaper, KMS checklist.
00:46:12 Maya: thanks. one ask — can you include sample audit output that shows deprovisioning events?
00:46:25 Marco: yes, sample will include timestamps and request IDs.

00:48:00 James: any concerns about cross-account S3 access? we prefer copy-to-bucket rather than granting write to third-party.
00:48:12 Marco: We typically recommend push-to-bucket via assume-role; but copy-to-bucket (we provide signed export) is also supported. We'll note options in the runbook.

00:50:30 Priya: final question — encryption at rest for model artifacts?
00:50:40 Marco: Model artifacts are encrypted with customer keys in Private; hosted uses service keys but we can do CMEK depending on plan.

00:52:10 Lena: Thanks everyone — we'll circulate notes and next steps.
00:52:25 Maya: thanks, bye.

End transcript.

References shared during call: SP metadata (link), SCIM-example.csv (link), RBAC-templates.xlsx (link), security-whitepaper.pdf (link), KMS-integration-checklist.md (link).
notes: Client emphasized SOC 2 retention and KMS ownership; agreed pilot + RBAC templates. Redwood to provide technical artifacts and schedule private network test.
technical_summary: SCIM v2 supported; Okta group->role mapping recommended; support for CMEK (Private) and hosted CMEK alias; audit export via S3/webhook; region routing by role binding.
